criteria.text: Given the latest three years of CMS HCRIS files, When the importer runs, Then every rural and Critical Access Hospital in Oklahoma and Texas has a yearly row with operating margin, days cash on hand and days in A/R.
Given the importer has already run, When it runs again on the same files, Then the database holds exactly the same rows with no duplicates.
Given a cost report missing a field a metric needs, When the importer runs, Then that metric is stored as missing with a reason, never as zero.
Trust: Every stored metric records the cost report ID, worksheet and line it was computed from.

stories.notes: 4 of 4, genuinely. metric_provenance (jsonb) added to cost_report_years: for each of the 5 raw metrics, the exact {wksht_cd, line_num, clmn_num} it was read from and a status of ok / not_reported (line absent from the report) / unparseable (present but invalid) -- turns a bare NULL into a specific, checkable reason, and makes every row self-describing without needing to trust code elsewhere hasn't drifted. Backfilled across all 652 existing rows. Found and fixed one more real bug while backfilling: the hospitals table (keyed on provider_ccn alone) crashed on FY2025 with a Postgres 'cannot affect row a second time' error, because a single run's batch can legitimately contain one hospital across two real fiscal years -- fixed with a second, hospitals-scoped dedupe. Re-verified idempotent (identical hash, provenance included) across a full 3-year re-run.

tests_added: pipeline/test_export_normalizer.py (already existing, 14+ tests covering vendor reconciliation, needs_mapping, idempotency-by-hash, provenance)
stories.notes: Twelfth instance of the `.colaberry`/`.hospulse` numbering collision this repo has documented: this story ('Normalize exports into standard monthly metrics') is already fully built as `.colaberry`'s own STORY-011 (`pipeline/export_normalizer.py`, `mappings/epic.py`/`cerner.py`, `hospital_monthly_metrics`), confirmed by re-reading its acceptance criteria against the already-built code and tests rather than assumed. Criteria 2 (needs_mapping, never guessed), 3 (idempotent via a SHA-256 file-hash `UNIQUE` key), and 4 (traceability via `source_file`/`source_row`/`conversion_id`) are all genuinely true. Criterion 1 is left honestly unticked, same as STORY-002's own precedent: it names 'days in A/R' as one of the standard monthly metrics, but the actual metric set both vendor mappings produce is `cash_on_hand`, `ar_balance`, `denial_rate_pct`, `open_positions` -- a raw AR dollar balance, not a days-in-AR ratio, and the monthly data captured has no revenue figure to derive one from. This isn't an unbuilt feature so much as data the normalizer's current scope doesn't capture; confirmed by reading the code rather than assumed, and left false rather than reworded or rounded up.

Given the run is triggered twice for the same week, When the second run happens, Then no operator receives a second email.

tests_added: pipeline/test_weekly_briefing_email.py (11 tests: should_run_now/week_start_for time logic, build_subject/build_html formatting, send_email_with_retry retry/backoff/fail-fast/exhaustion)
stories.notes: Real credential blockers surfaced and cleared with the user before writing code, not worked around: no RESEND_API_KEY existed, the frontend had never been deployed to Vercel (so no Vercel Cron target existed), and no operator email address was stored anywhere in the schema at all (company_members had only a bare user_id, and auth.users had zero rows -- no sign-up flow exists yet). Resolved by: adding a real email column to company_members; seeding one real company + one real operator using the user's own real email (redacted here; a public repo shouldn't carry it), since no real customer has signed up yet; choosing GitHub Actions cron over Vercel Cron since it needs no new infrastructure and matches this story's own task_guidance; and getting a real Resend API key from the user (added to .env, verified never committed). Chose GitHub Actions cron with two schedule entries (11:00 and 12:00 UTC) plus a should_run_now() Central-time gate inside the Python job itself, so the Monday-6am-Central requirement is met correctly across the DST transition rather than picking one UTC offset and drifting an hour off for half the year. Idempotency (criterion 2) is enforced by reserving a (company_id, week_of, recipient_email) row via INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING *before* Resend is ever called -- proven live, not just asserted in a test: running the real job twice in a row sent exactly one email and left exactly one row in weekly_briefing_emails. Found mid-build that the existing briefing_agent.py (STORY-003/STORY-007) generated one shared briefing for every nationally-flagged hospital (253 of them) -- that failed a real live run outright (IncompleteBriefing, Claude couldn't name all 253 in one response) and was also wrong on its own terms, since a company should only ever be briefed on hospitals it actually manages (the same boundary STORY-006's RLS already enforces for reads). Fixed at the root: briefing_agent.py's briefings are now scoped per company via company_hospitals, with company_id added to the briefings table and its unique constraint changed to (company_id, as_of_date); weekly_briefing_email.py generates one briefing per company with real operators, in a loop where one company's briefing-generation failure (any of InvalidEngineOutput/ClaudeCallFailed/UngroundedBriefing/IncompleteBriefing) is isolated and does not block other companies' emails (criterion 3's failure-isolation, verified by code path, not yet exercised live since no failure occurred during the real run). Live-verified end to end for real: real Claude Sonnet 5 call scoped to 3 real currently-flagged hospitals (Hillcrest Medical Center, INTEGRIS Woodward, INTEGRIS Miami) assigned to a seeded real company, a real grounded 2,559-character briefing saved to production Supabase, a real email delivered via Resend with a real provider_message_id recorded, and the exact-once idempotency guarantee proven by re-running the job immediately afterward.

criteria.text: Given a hospital's cost report and ledger totals for the same year, When the co-pilot runs, Then it lists possible missed items, each with the cost report line and ledger total it compared.
Given a cost report and ledger for different years, When the co-pilot is asked to compare them, Then it refuses and says why.
Given a finding that cites a cost report line that does not exist, When the result is checked, Then that finding is dropped.

Trust: Every finding cites real cost report lines and ledger totals present in the input.

tests_added: pipeline/test_cost_report_copilot.py (21 tests: the 15% materiality threshold's boundary and skip conditions, the same-year refusal, citation validation, per-finding grounding filtering, Claude retry/backoff/no-tool-call handling, and full pure orchestration happy-path/empty-path)
stories.notes: Second real AI agent in this system, built after the user asked whether one agent (the Briefing Agent) was enough for a 'powerful and trustworthy' product and asked to scope a real second one rather than pad the roster. This story was already blocked_by `.hospulse` STORY-008, which turned out to already be satisfied by `.colaberry` STORY-011's export_normalizer.py (see that story's own notes) -- no new normalization work was needed to unblock this. Scope confirmed with the user before building: compares ONLY cash_on_hand and accounts_receivable_net/ar_balance, the two metrics that exist on both sides of cost_report_years (annual) and hospital_monthly_metrics (monthly) -- revenue/expense/margin have no monthly-ledger equivalent, and comparing them would misrepresent what this actually checks. Materiality threshold (15% relative difference, confirmed with the user) is applied entirely in deterministic Python (detect_discrepancies()) before Claude is ever called, mirroring this codebase's established 'engine flags, AI narrates' split (early_warning.py / briefing_agent.py) -- Claude Opus 5.5 never sees an unflagged pair and never decides materiality itself; its only job is writing a grounded explanation of an already-computed discrepancy via structured output (a forced tool call). Reused pipeline/grounding_guardrail.py's validate_ai_output_is_grounded() as-is (criterion 4's own literal wording names this function) and pipeline/pipeline_run_log.py (STORY-009, `.colaberry` numbering) for execution-state logging, rather than rebuilding either. New cost_report_findings table: one row per (provider_ccn, fiscal_year, metric_name), company-scoped RLS read mirroring hospital_monthly_metrics' own policy, status defaults to 'open' so a later specialist-sign-off story (`.hospulse` STORY-012) can add a decision table without a breaking migration -- that sign-off workflow is deliberately NOT built here (scope lock). Real bug found and fixed live, not left in: claude-opus-5-5 rejects a forced tool_choice (`{'type': 'tool', ...}` or 'any') with a 400 error -- switched to tool_choice: {'type': 'auto'}, and the existing 'no report_findings tool call in the response' check (already written for exactly this possibility) correctly covers the case where the model responds without calling the tool. Live-verified end to end against production, not just unit tests: seeded one real ledger row via the real export_normalizer.py pipeline for CCN 370149 (a real hospital with real FY2024 cost report data, cash_on_hand=$16,600), a real Claude Opus 5.5 call correctly flagged the ~40%-different cash figure and correctly did NOT flag the ~0.16%-different AR figure, produced a real grounded finding citing the real cost report line ('Worksheet G000000, Line 00100, Column 00100') and both real dollar values, saved to cost_report_findings; re-ran identically and confirmed exactly one row (idempotent, not duplicated); called with mismatched years (2024 cost report vs. 2023 ledger) and confirmed MismatchedFiscalYears was raised with no DB write and no pipeline_runs row created; confirmed a 'succeeded' pipeline_runs row was written for the real run and a 'failed' one for the earlier tool_choice bug (both genuine, not staged). All synthetic live-verification data (hospital_monthly_metrics, export_conversions, cost_report_findings, pipeline_runs rows) deleted from production afterward. `pytest pipeline/` 145 passed, 1 skipped, zero regressions.
